STRICTLY CONFIDENTIAL • PROPRIETARY GOFAM CONTENT • INTERNAL DEVELOPMENT USE ONLY

This document is the implementation source for the GOFAM GROW Mission Engine. It contains 945 coded Missions across the seven public GOFAM categories, with three internal Sprout stages. The developer should implement the selection, replacement, completion, history and reward rules exactly as described here. The five internal Mission Groups within each Hill are implementation metadata only. Do not create descriptive names for these groups or expose them to users.
Total mission records in this specification: 945. Every category/stage contains 15 Missions per Hill and 105 Missions across seven Hills.
1. Resolve the user's category before Mission selection. Sprouts route silently by age to S1E, S1G or S1R.
2. Start with the user's Focus Hill. The bank for that Hill contains 15 Missions.
3. The 15 Missions are stored internally as five Mission Groups, each containing three Missions.
4. DEFAULT SELECTION MUST NOT choose all three Missions from the same Mission Group.
5. Preferred default: randomly choose THREE DIFFERENT Mission Groups out of the five, then randomly choose ONE eligible Mission from each chosen group.
6. Result: exactly three recommended Missions for the Hill, each from a different Mission Group.
7. Shuffle the display order of the three selected Missions. Do not show Group number, selection logic or hidden metadata.
8. Maximum active Missions for a Hill at any time = 3. Completing a Mission does not unlock a fourth Mission in the same cycle.

Default recommendations should favour variety. Maintain per-user, per-Hill Mission history. Recommended rule: select from the least-recently-surfaced eligible Missions first, while preserving three different Mission Groups whenever possible.
• Do not re-recommend a Mission that is currently active.
• Prefer Missions the user has never been offered before.
• After all 15 have been surfaced, recycle using least-recently-used order.
• If an eligibility or safety rule removes options, relax freshness before relaxing safety.
• Store both offered and completed history; a Mission the user repeatedly replaces should be deprioritised by future recommendation logic.
• The user may replace any ACTIVE, UNCOMPLETED Mission.
• When the user taps 'Change Mission', show the remaining eligible Missions from the same Hill, excluding the other active Missions.

• User choice is allowed to override group balance. The default recommendation is balanced; manual choice should be respected even if two or three chosen Missions come from the same internal Mission Group.
• Never allow more than 3 active Missions in the Hill.
• A completed Mission cannot be replaced in the current cycle.
• Store swap history: original Mission ID, replacement Mission ID, timestamp and number of swaps. This data will later help personalise recommendations.
• Do not penalise the user for changing a Mission.
• At cycle start, assign 3 Missions to the Focus Hill using the balanced selection logic above.
• Mission states: SUGGESTED -> ACTIVE -> COMPLETED. Optional secondary states: SWAPPED_OUT, EXPIRED, SKIPPED.
• Mark completion only after an explicit user action such as 'Complete Mission' / 'We Did It'.
• Once 3/3 active Missions for the Hill are completed, mark the Hill's Mission set COMPLETE for that cycle.
• For Early Sprouts, completion belongs operationally to the caregiver. Never frame an incomplete Mission as the child's failure.
• For Growing Sprouts, use shared parent-child language. For Ready Sprouts onward, progressively shift ownership toward the child/user.

Keep rewards server-configurable. Current GOFAM configuration for the Focus Hill: +5 Coins for each Mission completed; +15 bonus Coins when all 3 Missions are completed in the cycle; +1 Hill Step for completing 3/3. The app should calculate rewards from configuration rather than hard-coded UI logic.

The Focus Hill receives the default set of three Missions. If the product allows users to explore other Hills, apply the same 15-Mission bank and maximum-3-active rule independently to each Hill. Reward and Step behaviour for non-Focus Hills should remain configuration-driven.
• Never recommend a Mission outside the user's developmental category/stage.
• Respect physical ability, health limitations and accessibility where user data makes them known.
• Health Missions must not diagnose, prescribe medication or replace professional medical care.
• Money Missions must not require a minimum income, investment, debt or purchase.
• Relationship Missions must not pressure reconciliation with unsafe or harmful relationships.
• Boundary Missions should support appropriate limits and trusted-adult escalation for children.
• Sprout Missions must be age-appropriate and caregiver-safe; never use forced waiting, forced affection, food pressure or unsafe physical challenges.
• Do not require public posting, disclosure of private information, or proof that would create privacy risk.
• Mission text may be localised, but the underlying Mission ID and intended behavioural action must remain stable.

Future premium AI Missions should use the same Mission Engine contracts. AI may personalise wording, context, difficulty and timing, but a generated Mission must be mapped server-side to one Hill and one internal Mission Group before being eligible for recommendation.
• AI-generated Missions must pass age/stage, safety, feasibility and duplication checks.
• AI should use GAP results, Mission history, completion behaviour, replacements, user preferences and current context where available.
• Do not expose internal Mission Group labels to the user.
• Generated Missions should remain small, concrete, observable and realistically completable.
• Prefer the next-best Mission that addresses an underrepresented group within the user's current Hill unless the user's behaviour/preferences indicate otherwise.
• Store generation model/version, prompt version, Mission Group, Hill, generated text and completion outcome for auditability.
